ai_show_review.summary: Brief five‑minute Viola Lee Blues fragment; rest of set missing
ai_show_review.blurb: The recording captures a short, decent‑sounding instrumental take of Viola Lee Blues. Only two songs appear and the remainder of the performance is absent. Sound quality is good but the source may not be the Dead.
ai_show_review.review: What unfolds at California Hall on Halloween night 1966 is more mystery than milestone. The sole surviving fragment – a crisp, five‑minute instrumental run through Viola Lee Blues – showcases tight interplay, yet it stops abruptly, leaving Alice D. Millionaire and any further material lost to history. The soundboard capture (gd1966-10-31.sbd.bershaw.5416.shnf) is clear and well‑balanced, but experts suspect the musicians may not be the Grateful Dead at all, which clouds its value for completists. For those intrigued by early San Francisco psychedelic scenes, it offers a glimpse of the era’s raw energy, but listeners should temper expectations about authenticity and completeness.

best_recording.reason: Only available soundboard; clear audio despite uncertainty about the performers
